posts.name: Piyush Singh
posts.cooked:
@Mrinal.exe , @21f3000759
I created a setup.sh script (with the help of an LLM) to make it easier for me to solve BPT1 problems, since I find it difficult to read the question and write code in the same terminal at the same time.
Is it allowed to use such a pre-written setup script during OPPE exams, or is it considered restricted?

Screenshot 2026-04-15 at 10.10.59 AM1308×1226 121 KB

posts.name: Ishan Shishodiya
posts.cooked: Usage of tmux is allowed in BPTs and OPPEs. You don’t need to create a custom setup just to use tmux, you can check tmux_Hotkeys.md · GitHub for a cheatsheet on tmux hotkeys.

posts.name: Piyush Singh
posts.cooked:
Thank you for the clarification
Since tmux usage is allowed in OPPEs, can I use my setup.sh file just to automatically start and configure tmux instead of setting it up manually every time?

posts.name: Ishan Shishodiya
posts.cooked:
I won’t recommend that. During OPPEs copying and pasting external scripts can be viewed as cheating and be flagged by the proctor or the screen monitoring system.

It’s better if you use hotkeys instead.

  • tmux to run tmux
  • Ctrl + b, % to split the windows vertically into panes
  • Ctrl + b, <- to go to the left pane
  • Ctrl + b, -> to go to the right pane
22f2001554:

you can check tmux_Hotkeys.md · GitHub

Note - First press Ctrl + b then press any of the hotkeys given in the gist.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Hopefully you have gone through the video on TMUX in portal.

Link: https://seek.study.iitm.ac.in/courses/ns_26t1_se2001?id=207

You are expected to be familiar with tmux. Yes you can use tmux, you can also configure the tmux.conf file as per your requirement (an example is given in the video objectives).

During OPPE, the VM will grant you login access one hour before the exam starts (at 5pm), at that moment you can go ahead and configure any user settings you want such as this tmux configuration, or .bashrc aliases and shortcuts. You can also scp this script if you want (but looking at your script, I dont find it scalable, better to configure your tmux conf correctly instead) before the exam starts.

You can find .bashrc tips and tricks here.

posts.name: Diptanshu Suraj dube
posts.cooked: Is the SC oppe conducted on VM or the seek portal? where is this mentioned can someone tell me?

posts.name: Gurkirat Singh
posts.cooked:
24f3000618:

Is the SC oppe conducted on VM or the seek portal?

On another topic

You have to solve the OPPE questions on OPPE vm (similar in design & everything to course vm only difference is that it has a different hostname). Access will be given one week before OPPE and you can do NPPE (mock exam), there to check for any issues.

TA replied on a similar doubt.

posts.name: Diptanshu Suraj dube
posts.cooked: Thanks! I didn’t know that they should mention this in some doc(grading policy or some thing so that the students don’t get confused.

posts.name: Baskaran Nadar
posts.cooked:
Is VM different from the one that we currently use?

If so, do we need to generate a new public key using ssh-keygen for the new server and save it in server before the exam starts ?

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked:
Baskaran_Nadar:

Is VM different from the one that we currently use?

Yes, OPPE VM will be different.

Baskaran_Nadar:

If so, do we need to generate a new public key using ssh-keygen for the new server and save it in server before the exam starts ?

No, you don’t have to generate new public key. You can paste your existing public key (will show the process in Friday’s TA session). You will get access to it 1 week before to check if everything is working fine & you have to do NPPE (mock) there.

posts.name: Baskaran Nadar
posts.cooked: Do we have access to the cheat sheets provided in the seek portal for Bash, sed & awk ?

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: No. You can refer to man and info pages.

posts.name: Diptanshu Suraj dube
posts.cooked: will the cheat sheet be entirely unavaliable this time?

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked: Cheatsheets will not be present in exam portal and accessing them will be treated as malpractice.

posts.name: Diptanshu Suraj dube
posts.cooked: got it thank you for the reply

posts.name: Baskaran Nadar
posts.cooked:
@sayan

image1363×727 69.3 KB

I use WSL/Ubuntu terminal to login VM. Instead of VMs tmux, I prefer the split option of WSL which allows me to view two terminal side by side and supports mouse.

Yes, that would mean I will have two login sessions in VM; even under tmux, it would amount to be multiple sessions.

Can I continue to use this split screen or do you guy want me to start learning those keystrokes for tmux ?

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked: Yes, you can use but tmux is encouraged!

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: Also, tmux provides the added advantage that if you lose your network connection mid exam, your unsaved changes in script file will not be lost, you can simply re-ssh and do tmux a to attach to last session.
